headline: Instagram Reels will be adopted widely as the default TikTok replacement despite persistent complaints about lost 'vibe' and higher effort, especially among low-income rural women.
say_do_gap: People say they miss TikTok's vibe and find Instagram more effort (only 49% supportive), but 71% intend to adopt and 48% to share — complaining while migrating.
summary: Reels captures the TikTok vacuum: adoption intent holds at 71% across rounds while opposition halves from 41% to 17%. Urban, higher-income men drive enthusiasm (92% adopt), but even low-income rural users adopt at 62% because Reels costs no extra data or app install. The only hard resistance is Northeast (tiny sample) and low-income women who prefer YouTube Shorts.

drivers.explanation: 45% cite 'TikTok replacement convenience' — users across segments need a frictionless substitute inside an app they already have.
30% cite 'Cost and data savings' — <₹15k users adopt at 63% despite only +0.15 net sentiment; no new download is decisive.

drivers.factor: Missing TikTok 'vibe' and higher creation friction
drivers.explanation: 15% nostalgia + 10% privacy themes — low-income women (homemakers, agri labourers) say Instagram 'effort zyada lagga' and will try Shorts instead.
Urban adopt 92% (net +0.80), >₹75k adopt 100% — they seed content that pulls rural users in.

segments_at_risk.why: Net sentiment barely positive (+0.15), adopt 63% but vocal about missing TikTok's algorithm and ease; they are the Shorts-switching risk.
Only negative net (-0.38) and 25% adopt — possible cultural/language mismatch in Explore feed; monitor for early churn.

surprise: The steepest income gradient in adoption (63% → 100%) coexists with the flattest sentiment gradient (+0.15 → +1.20) — poor users adopt despite lukewarm feelings because the switching cost is zero.
